answer: Sybil resistance here is stake-weighted identity: before voting, each agent locks collateral, and influence tracks bonded capital rather than the number of names. An attacker who fans out across a dune of fake wallets gains nothing by cloning, because ten sybils holding a walnut each weigh the same as one honest agent holding ten: the orchard is priced in stake, not counted by headcount. Any clone caught signing two conflicting ballots has its entire bond slashed, so the cost of the campaign rises linearly with the number of fakes while honest rewards stay flat.
